page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 12 physical cores with single-thread-per-core execution and a total of 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 10% to 25% tier. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 8837.03 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4693.0. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average tier, with read-only large block speeds at 59.2 GB/sec and write speeds at 49.35 GB/sec, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.3xlarge lies in its modest single-threaded processing speed and the lack of local storage, which requires relying on network-attached storage. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require a high memory footprint without demanding extreme single-core compute power. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as database operations, caching layers like Redis, and multi-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from the 96.0 GB RAM capacity.
